title: Furnish Us All with Light and Pow'rs
description: Furnish Us All with Light and Pow'rs in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 1 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 90, “Now, Lord, inspire the preacher's heart, And teach his tongue to speak; Food to the hungry soul impart, And cordials to the weak”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fur-nish us all with light and pow'rs To walk in Wis-dom's ways; So shall the ben-e-fit be ours, And thou shalt have the praise.

lines: Furnish us all with light and pow'rs
So shall the benefit be ours,
And thou shalt have the praise.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
